Interface OidcClientEndpoint

public interface OidcClientEndpoint
Describes one redirect URI a client is registered for, and what it may do through it.

A client registers an endpoint per redirect URI rather than a bare list of URIs, so the keys a token is signed and encrypted with, and the resources the token may be used against, can differ between a client's environments or deployments without registering a separate client for each.

Property names use lower case with underscores, so getRedirectUri() reads redirect_uri and getEncryptJwk() reads encrypt_jwk.

  • Method Details

    • getAuthorization

      Iterable<OidcClientAuthorization> getAuthorization()
      Gets how a client redeeming a code issued to this endpoint authenticates itself at the token endpoint.

      Registered per endpoint rather than per client, so one deployment's key can be rotated or revoked without disturbing another's.

      More than one record may be registered; the first that accepts the presented credential is used, which is what lets an old and a new credential both be honored while one is being rotated in. An endpoint with no record at all — null or empty — accepts nothing, including a public request with no credential; a record that carries no key is what registers an endpoint as public.

      Returns:
      authorization records, tried in order; null or empty to accept no credential at all

    • getAccessRoles

      Iterable<String> getAccessRoles()
      Gets the identity roles that entitle an end user to a token from this endpoint at all.

      Checked against the effective principal — the impersonated principal when a backdoor request is honored, otherwise the one the identity provider authenticated. Holding any one is enough. null or empty denies every principal; the literal role ALL is what registers an endpoint as open to anyone, since a role check treats it as matching unconditionally.

      Returns:
      identity role names; null or empty to admit no one

    • getBackdoorRoles

      Iterable<String> getBackdoorRoles()
      Gets the identity roles that entitle a principal to request another principal's token through the impersonated_principal request parameter.

      Checked against the principal the identity provider actually authenticated, never the one being impersonated, so holding a backdoor role is what lets a principal act as someone else rather than something the target of impersonation grants. Only honored outside a production deployment; a request naming one in production is answered as if it had named none, whether or not the authenticated principal holds a backdoor role. null or empty denies the backdoor to every principal; ALL opens it to anyone, the same as getAccessRoles().

      Returns:
      identity role names; null or empty to refuse impersonation to everyone

    • getRoles

    • getResources

      Iterable<OidcClientResource> getResources()
      Gets the resources a request through this endpoint may act on.

      The requested resource selects among these, and the scopes the matching entries declare are what the request may ask for. An entry with no URI is the one a request naming no resource matches.

      Returns:
      resources
